answer.literal_rules: library-literal accepts one distinct operand of 1..1024 UTF-16 code units. It preserves whitespace, newlines, and case without normalization and checks for an ordinal substring of each decoded string-literal use in selected implementation libraries. Repeating the identical operand collapses; distinct operands conflict. The empty values list is not an allow list: any decoded UTF-16 text within these constraints is accepted. 600 astral Unicode characters occupy 1200 UTF-16 code units, so that operand is rejected.
answer.literal_prerequisites: Use --tfm net8.0 to select one exact NuGet target framework; library-literal and --tfm require each other. This facet requires package-content acquisition and a package-content provider. An exact package ID admits at most one candidate; this facet permits no more than five package candidates.
answer.dependency_rules: Without dependency-depth, depends=Newtonsoft.Json matches direct dependencies only. With dependency-depth=3, the exact depends predicate matches direct or transitive declaration paths through a maximum of three declaration edges. The legacy depends-transitive=Newtonsoft.Json spelling with depth 3 matches only edges at depths 2 through 3, so a direct-only hit is excluded. Repeated exact dependency terms are ANDed and share traversal. The allowed dependency-depth values are 2, 3, and 4; depth 1 is invalid. Traversal requires an explicit dependency-target=<tfm>, so dependency-target=all is invalid for the second command. A starts-with depends predicate remains direct and cannot alone authorize depth.
answer.dependency_prerequisites: The dependency predicate uses nuspec acquisition. dependency-depth requires an exact depends or legacy depends-transitive term and an explicit dependency-target=net8.0. An exact package ID admits one candidate; depth queries permit at most five candidates.
